doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Lydian book publication and marriage to Juanita
title: Worries about repeating stories, and the book's first publication in 1953
summary: Russell asks whether his stories could bother relatives; Daughtry recaps the check and the 1953 publication.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I have to ask you a question that occurred to me. I’m telling these things. If they get out, is there a problem? Would there be a problem with, say, some of the relatives of these people I’m talking about?
He had to learn how to talk again.

So we have a situation where you open your door one day, there’s an envelope, and in it is a check from Dave Guard for $5,000, which, back then, fast forwarding to today, that would be like $50,000, $100,000. That was a lot of money. I got excited when you mentioned it. I can imagine how you must have been at that time, particularly since it meant the bringing to fruition – of at least the first stage of fruition – your life work, your dream.
I was able to do that with that money.
I’ve seen a date of ’53 as the first publishing of The Lydian.
So that coincides with that time.
Yeah. Eventually Buckwheat recovered. He was extremely embarrassed by it. I think – well, he certainly learned a lesson. But he also passed away young. So all those people, somehow they died young.
You were still managing, at this point, to not drive the cab.
You were still taking Gil’s advice and sticking with your musical pursuits.
